title: Law Enforcement and Other Matters Bill
what_it_is: Law Enforcement and Other Matters Bill

sections.label: Scam cases rise 2023
sections.summary: There were over 46,000 cases in 2023, a nearly 50% increase from 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: There were over 46,000 cases in 2023, a nearly 50% increase from 2022.

sections.label: SMS scam fall after implementation
sections.summary: In the three months after its implementation, scams due to SMSes fell by 70%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the three months after its implementation, scams due to SMSes fell by 70%.

sections.label: Scam losses local mobile lines
sections.summary: In 2023, about $400 million were lost from scam and cybercrime cases involving local mobile lines.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2023, about $400 million were lost from scam and cybercrime cases involving local mobile lines.

sections.label: Irresponsible subscriber deemed liable scenarios
sections.summary: An irresponsible subscriber will be deemed liable in three scenarios involving giving away a local SIM card for gain or not taking reasonable steps.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To address the challenge that the Police face today in proving knowledge or criminal intent, an irresponsible subscriber will be deemed liable in the following scenarios: one, the irresponsible subscriber gave away the local SIM card for any gain; two, he did not take reasonable steps to find out the identity and physical location of the recipient of the local SIM card; or three, he did not take reasonable steps to find out the recipient's purpose for obtaining the local SIM card.

sections.label: Bill offences target middlemen
sections.summary: The Bill introduces offences in sections 39D and 39F under the MOA to target middlemen.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces offences in sections 39D and 39F under the MOA to target middlemen.

sections.label: Deemed liability for local SIM cards
sections.summary: A person who receives, supplies or possesses local SIM cards may be deemed liable without proof of knowledge or criminal intent in two stated situations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To address the evidentiary challenge that Police face today, a person who receives, supplies or possesses such local SIM cards may be deemed liable, without the Prosecution having to prove knowledge or criminal intent, if the local SIM cards were used for crime; or 11 or more local SIM cards were found in the middleman's possession.

sections.label: Local SIM cards in scams
sections.summary: A sampling study of about 1,400 local SIM cards used in scams in the second half of 2023 found about 65% were sold by nine retailers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In a sampling study of around 1,400 local SIM cards used in scams in the second half of 2023, we found that about 65% of such SIM cards were sold by just nine retailers.

sections.label: New section 39G for retailers
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a new section 39G to target errant retailers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As such, the Bill introduces a new section 39G to target errant retailers.

sections.label: Penalties for SIM card offences
sections.summary: The offences carry fines of up to $10,000 or up to three years' imprisonment, or both, with higher penalties for repeat offences.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The offences for irresponsible registrants will carry a fine of up to $10,000 or imprisonment of up to three years, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The offences of receiving, supplying and possessing local SIM cards and facilitating fraudulent registrations of local SIM cards, will carry a fine of up to $10,000 or imprisonment of up to three years, or both, for a first offence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For a second or subsequent offence, the penalty will be a fine of up to $20,000 or imprisonment of up to five years, or both.

sections.label: Extraterritorial SIM card offences
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a new section 39H to the MOA to allow the new SIM card offences to apply extraterritorially where there is a proven link to harm in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Bill also introduces a new section 39H to the MOA to allow the new SIM card offences to apply extraterritorially, as long as there is a proven link to harm in Singapore.

sections.label: High Court on MHCTA apprehensions
sections.summary: Police apprehended him under the MHCTA and brought him to IMH, but the High Court determined the danger had to be imminent, in hours rather than days.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Police apprehended him under the MHCTA and brought him to the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) for medical treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: However, in a recent judgment, the High Court made a determination that for apprehensions under the MHCTA, the danger presented had to be imminent and it had to be in a matter of hours rather than days.

sections.label: Clause 13 amends MHCTA
sections.summary: Clause 13 amends the MHCTA to allow the Police to apprehend the person in such situations to take them for medical treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 13 therefore amends the MHCTA to allow the Police to apprehend the person in such situations to take them for medical treatment.

sections.label: Police powers during apprehensions
sections.summary: Clause 14 amends the Police Force Act so search and seizure powers are available to Police when making apprehensions under the MHCTA or other Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 14 therefore amends the Police Force Act to make clear that relevant powers, such as those of search and seizure, are available to the Police when making apprehensions, whether under the MHCTA or any other Acts.

sections.label: Police may not take further action
sections.summary: Clause 6 amends the Criminal Procedure Code to let Police not take further action for non-arrestable offences if not serious or grounds insufficient.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill amends the Criminal Procedure Code to enable the Police to not take further action for non-arrestable offences in two circumstances – one, if the case is not of a serious nature, or two, if there are insufficient grounds for proceeding with the matter.

sections.label: CNB, ICA, GRA bail powers
sections.summary: Clauses 5 and 7 to 12 allow CNB, ICA and GRA officers to grant bail or personal bond for arrested persons.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 5 and clauses 7 to 12 allow officers from the Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB), Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) and Gambling Regulatory Authority (GRA) to grant bail or personal bond for arrested persons.

sections.label: Detention in immigration depots
sections.summary: The amendments allow persons arrested under the National Registration Act and Passports Act to be detained in immigration depots instead of Police stations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments also allow persons arrested under the National Registration Act and the Passports Act to be detained in immigration depots, such as ICA Building, Tuas Checkpoint and Woodlands Checkpoint, instead of bringing them to Police stations.

sections.label: YRSG symbol misuse penalties
sections.summary: The Bill amends the SCORE Act to give YRSG exclusive rights to its symbols, with misuse punishable by fine, imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To safeguard the symbols and ensure that they are not misused, the Bill amends the SCORE Act, to give YRSG the exclusive right to the use of YRSG's symbols and symbols of initiatives related to YRSG's mission.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Those who misuse these symbols will be liable for prosecution and could face a fine of up to $10,000 or imprisonment of up to six months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the case of a continuing offence, the offender could be further fined up to $250 for every day or part of a day during which the offence continues after conviction.

sections.label: Scam increase and SIM groups
sections.summary: From 2022 to 2023 scam cases rose 46.8%, and the Bill targets three groups involved in facilitating scams through SIM cards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: From 2022 to 2023, there was a 46.8% increase in scam cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Bill targets three key groups involved in facilitating scams: those irresponsibly registering local SIM cards or Group A; those possessing or supplying SIM cards or Group B; and retailers facilitating fraudulent SIM card registration or Group C.

sections.label: Proposed penalties for offenders
sections.summary: The proposed penalties include fines of up to $10,000 and/or imprisonment, with harsher penalties for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The proposed penalties for offenders include fines of up to $10,000 and/or imprisonment, with harsher penalties for repeat offenders.

sections.label: Apprehension on reasonable belief
sections.summary: The proposed amendments would allow apprehension based on a reasonable belief of potential harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments would allow apprehension based on a "reasonable belief" of potential harm.

sections.label: Clause 13 amends MHCTA
sections.summary: Clause 13 amends section 7 of the Mental Health Care and Treatment Act 2008 by reducing the threshold for police to apprehend a person.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 13 of the Bill amends section 7 of the Mental Health Care and Treatment Act 2008, or MHCTA, by reducing the threshold requirement for a police or special police officer to exercise the power to apprehend a person.

sections.label: New apprehension power and sub-clause
sections.summary: The amendment empowers police to apprehend a person believed to endanger peace or safety, requiring only reasonably likely danger, not imminent actual harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The new amendment proposed in this Bill supersedes the High Court's interpretation by empowering Police and special police officers to apprehend a person, P, if they believe that P may endanger peace or any other person's life or personal safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It would also introduce a new sub-clause (2), subsection (aa), which provides that it is sufficient that the danger to life or personal safety is only reasonably likely to occur and need not be imminent and actual harm is not required.

sections.label: CRPD Committee recommendation to Singapore
sections.summary: The CRPD Committee urged Singapore to repeal legislative provisions allowing involuntary deprivation of liberty of persons with disabilities on grounds of impairment or perceived dangerousness.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At paragraph 30A of the concluding observations in respect of Article 14 of the CRPD on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities to Liberty, the CRPD Committee urged Singapore to repeal all legislative provisions allowing for the involuntary deprivation of liberty of persons with intellectual disabilities and persons with psychosocial disabilities on the grounds of their impairment or their perceived dangerousness to themselves or others.

sections.label: Question on MHCTA position
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government confirms its position on the MHCTA remains the same despite the CRPD Committee's recommendation to reform the law.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Can the Government confirm if this position on the MHCTA remains the same, notwithstanding the CRPD Committee's recommendation for this House to reform this law?

sections.label: Detention risk assessment time frames
sections.summary: Asks whether time frames apply to assessing detention under the new reasonable risk to safety threshold.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With the introduction of the new threshold of reasonable risk to safety, can the Minister confirm if there would be any time frames that are applied to the assessment of whether to detain?

sections.label: Expanding Crisis Response Team programme
sections.summary: Asks if the Government will expand the CRT programme beyond suicide risk to general mental health crises.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A 2023 journal article published in European Psychiatry found that CRT intervention could mitigate suicide risk and pressure on the mental health system, that is, reduce unnecessary emergency room visits and hospital admissions, create greater mental health awareness and facilitate individuals' connection to mental health care services, that is, in hospitals or the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given the positive impact of the CRT, has the Government considered expanding the programme to respond not only to cases involving the risk of suicide but also persons experiencing mental health crises more generally?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In response to a PQ in March 2022, the Minister for Home Affairs had stated that the Police and other investigative agencies' primary task is to deter crime, investigate and deal with crime, and they are not deeply trained in mental health issues.

sections.label: Beyond the Label Collective launch
sections.summary: The National Council of Social Service launched the Beyond the Label Collective in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For this, the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) launched the Beyond the Label Collective in 2022.

sections.label: Mental health training for emergency volunteers
sections.summary: Proposes expanding Community Life-Saving Programme courses and training CERT volunteers to respond to mental health crises.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Currently, the Community Life-Saving Programme, offered jointly by the People's Association and MHA, offers the standard First Aid plus AED Awareness Course, SFAA and the CPR AED certification.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This can be expanded to include the Singapore Emergency Responder Academy's First Aid and Mental Health Training Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Volunteers with the People's Association Community Emergency Response Team should also attend such training so that they are able to respond to persons experiencing mental health crises.

sections.label: Mobile lines and scam losses
sections.summary: Local mobile lines implicated in scams quadrupled in two years, with victims losing $384 million in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The number of local mobile lines implicated in scams and other cybercrimes has quadrupled in just two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This worrying trend is reflected in the financial losses as well, with victims losing nearly triple the amount in 2023 – a staggering $384 million compared to $137 million in 2021.

sections.label: Bill targeting SIM card misuse
sections.summary: Asks how the Bill will target family members, relatives, caregivers and persons exploiting close contact with vulnerable elderly to register SIM cards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will this Bill target family members, relatives, caregivers and persons who exploit their close contact with vulnerable elderly, in misusing their identity to register SIM cards?

sections.label: Lowered apprehension threshold for mental disorder
sections.summary: The threshold for apprehending a mentally disordered individual is lowered to reasonable suspicion when possible harm is reasonably likely, not only imminent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In particular, the lowering of the threshold before a mentally disordered individual may be apprehended to one of reasonable suspicion, when an act of possible harm is reasonably likely to occur and not only when it is imminent and mental disorder is suspected.

sections.label: Safeguards against Police power misuse
sections.summary: The Court acknowledged Police discretion but highlighted the need for responsible action, raising the question of safeguards against officers overstepping authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While the law empowers Police to apprehend individuals believed to be a danger to themselves or others due to mental health concerns, it is critical to have safeguards against misuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Court acknowledged the importance of Police discretion in such situations, but also highlighted the need for responsible action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This case raises the question: what safeguards are in place to prevent Police officers from overstepping their authority, as seen in the Mah Kiat Seng case?

sections.label: Police discretion on non-arrestable offenses
sections.summary: Part 2 clause 6 empowers the Police to decide against pursuing non-arrestable offenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Additionally, part 2 clause 6 empowers the Police to decide against pursuing non-arrestable offenses.

sections.label: Protecting seniors' SIM registration identities
sections.summary: The House is urged to establish clear guidelines addressing misuse of seniors' identities for SIM card registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, to maximise its effectiveness, I urge the House to consider the following: first, protect vulnerable populations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must establish clear guidelines to address the misuse of seniors' identities for SIM card registration.

sections.label: Urgent apprehension of suicide risk
sections.summary: The Bill gives Police latitude to act with urgency on reasonable grounds of suicide risk, supported by structured training and specialist input.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Time is of the essence and where reasonable grounds are sufficiently present to suggest a potential threat to self and others, my view is that apprehension may be necessary to save a life under such circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill, Mr Speaker, gives some latitude for Police officers to act with some urgency and not reactively, before a suicide attempt becomes imminent and before rescue could be more risky, both for the person who is under duress and for those who are trying to make a genuine attempt at rescue.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where suicide risk assessment, even for psychiatrists, is not a perfect science, my view is that it is fair and appropriate for Police officers to exercise reasonable judgement without waiting for a suicide to be imminently clear or after such attempt at lethal harm has been actualised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Structured training for Police officers in the apprehension of attempted suicide cases would be important to guide Police officers fronting such work, and this could be coupled with considered inputs from care professionals and specialists in the field.

sections.label: Expedient assessment after apprehension
sections.summary: For apprehensions under subsections 26A to 26F, the Ministry must ensure individuals are sent for formal assessment without delay.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where the apprehension is done under subsections 26A to 26F of the Police Force Act, the Ministry must then ensure that the individuals are sent for a formal assessment by a medical practitioner or a designated medical practitioner at a psychiatric institution under the sections 9 and 10 of the MHTCA with expedience and without delay.

sections.label: Mental health and law enforcement collaboration
sections.summary: The Ministry could study closer collaboration between mental health professionals and law enforcement, including combined first-responder teams for crisis calls involving mentally disordered individuals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I think there is scope for the Ministry to study the prospect of closer collaboration between mental health professionals and law enforcement especially when dealing with crisis calls relating to mentally disordered individuals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There could be value in having combined teams of law enforcement and mental health practitioners as collaborative first responders to ensure that, on one hand, there is Police resource for swift apprehension to safety of such individuals where required and if the threshold is not met and care can be safely given, mental health professionals, in turn, could be the ones offering supportive care thereafter.

sections.label: Police powers in psychiatric emergencies
sections.summary: Police and Civil Defence officers should be empowered to act in psychiatric emergencies, while physical crime fell and scam and cybercrime cases rose.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, in the face of a psychiatric emergency, where there is an active threat or concern over suicide, a danger to life either imminent or reasonably anticipated, the work of our Police officers and their Civil Defence counterpart remain important.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Within reasonable grounds, my view is that they should be empowered to exercise appropriate means to perform such a lifesaving role, before any ensuing treatment can be administered accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While physical crime cases have declined over the past five years, from 23,980 cases in 2019 to 19,966 cases in 2023, the reverse has happened for scam and cybercrime cases, rising almost five times from 11,135 cases in 2019 to 50,376 cases in 2023, with the increase seen last year the largest annual increase yet, at 16,707 cases or an almost 50% jump compared to the year before.

sections.label: Presumption over local SIM cards
sections.summary: Section 39B presumes reasonable grounds to believe a local SIM card would be used to commit or facilitate a crime, with a fine or imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under section 39B, it would be presumed that a person has reasonable grounds to believe, that the local SIM card would be used to commit or facilitate a crime and until the contrary is proved, could be found guilty of an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or both.

sections.label: Retailer and licensee liability under section 39G
sections.summary: Section 39G makes it an offence for retailers or telecommunication licensees to register SIM cards without authorisation or with false particulars, and asks about licensee and management liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I welcome section 39G, which makes it an offence for a retailer or telecommunication licensee to register a local SIM card using any person's particulars without that person's authorisation or knowing the particulars were false or misleading under certain conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We have certainly seen cases in the past, where errant retailers were taken to task; such as earlier this year, where an authorised dealer was fined $48,000 for exploiting customers' personal data to register SIM cards without their knowledge or consent, making an estimated profit of $35,000 along the way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, just as we censure financial institutions for not putting in place adequate Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing measures, to what extent does the buck stop at the retailers and authorised dealers themselves; and when would the telecommunication licensee itself be liable for failing to prevent, detect and address such abuses of their SIM cards and telecommunications networks to facilitate crime?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Beyond employees of retailers or the mobile service providers, who may have been directly involved in facilitating the SIM card registrations, to what extent would the management team and the board of these companies be liable themselves under the new section 39G, especially since the employees of these mobile service providers are specifically identified as such?

sections.label: Publicity on SIM card offences
sections.summary: After the Law Enforcement and Other Matters Bill, certain SIM card acts can be criminal offences, and the Government is urged to conduct more publicity campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After the passing of the Law Enforcement and Other Matters Bill, providing personal information to strangers for the registration of local SIM cards, selling SIM cards registered under one's own or another person's name, or receiving, supplying or possessing someone else's SIM card without proper justification can constitute criminal offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Many of us may intuitively know that providing one’s identity to dishonest companies as a phantom employee to earn CPF funds, or handing over one’s bank accounts to strangers to help unscrupulous individuals abuse the accounts, or even facilitating money laundering activities, are all illegal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, many people may not realise the significant harm that can result from providing one’s identity to strangers for the registration of local SIM cards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I urge the Government to conduct more publicity campaigns on this topic to protect our fellow citizens who may unwittingly commit an offense, such as the elderly and those with diminished mental capacity.

sections.label: Mandatory police training for enforcers
sections.summary: The speaker calls for the Singapore Police Force to make its training on recognising, managing and diffusing such situations mandatory for all enforcers, including NSFs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It was, after all, a whole store of people against one N.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I later found out that our Police Force are indeed trained to recognise, manage and diffuse such situations and I call for the Singapore Police Force (SPF) to ensure that such training be made mandatory for all enforcers, NSFs included, if it if not already done so and this should be conducted in a timely and frequent manner.

sections.label: Mental health amendment and awareness
sections.summary: The amendment limits police power and aims to make Singaporeans aware of people with amplified needs, following a 2024 mental health Motion and 2023 national strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Better yet, if most of the commuters have a basic understanding on how to help someone in a meltdown situation, the Police may not even have to be involved in the first place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This particular amendment clearly is not here to vest more power for law enforcement to make arrests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It sets clear limits to their power so that we can make the Police Force a force for the nation, to make Singapore the safest place in the world, if I may quote the SPF's vision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: More importantly, the heart of this amendment is not to correct behaviours, but to make more Singaporeans aware of people with amplified needs, so that the whole kampung can come together and make a home for us in this city.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In February 2024, this Parliament overwhelmingly passed a landmark Motion on advancing mental health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This House recognised the importance of mental health as a health, social and economic issue and called for a whole-of-Singapore effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This followed the October 2023 launch of the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy.

sections.label: Custody before harm occurs
sections.summary: Under the proposed new law, police may take someone into custody when danger to life or personal safety is reasonably likely, before actual harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the proposed new law, as long as the danger to human life or personal safety is reasonably likely to occur, police officers will be allowed to take someone into custody before any actual harm is caused.

sections.label: Scaling up first-line response
sections.summary: The passage asks whether such responses should be scaled up as the first line of response to individuals in mental health crises, letting law enforcement focus on primary duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Should we therefore scale these up so that as far as possible this will be the first line of response to individuals in mental health crises thus enabling law enforcement officers to focus on their primary duties?

sections.label: Training MHA personnel
sections.summary: It says autistic and ADHD people are neurodivergent and more likely to have confrontations with the law, and asks for MHA personnel training in mental health assessment and de-escalation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Autism spectrum and ADHD folk are considered neurodivergent and more likely to have confrontations with the law as they do not know how to back down, or sometimes, cannot." With resources available in Singapore, it would be good to see all MHA personnel, within a year if the Bill passes, given some training in assessing the various types of mental health conditions and skills to de-escalate and bring them to a safe place.

sections.label: Assurance on rights
sections.summary: The passage asks for assurance that passing the Bill will not diminish rights or disrupt day-to-day living because a member of the public seeks Police intervention prematurely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can we get an assurance that nothing in the passing of this Bill will diminish their rights or be disrupted in day-to-day living because a member of the public chooses to seek the intervention of the Police prematurely?

sections.label: Effort of matured community
sections.summary: The passage states the latter may take more effort, time and resources, reflecting an enlightened and matured community rather than one focused only on expedience and efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Admittedly, the latter may take more effort, time, and resources – but that is the reflection of an enlightened and matured community and not just one that focuses only on expedience and efficiency.

sections.label: Delay law until police trained
sections.summary: Speaker suggests delaying the new law until Home Team officers are trained in basic mental health knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If this House passes this Bill, I can see the silver lining should we consider the following.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I see a silver lining in a better equipped law enforcement team, because we will also train them in basic knowledge of mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, could we delay implementation of the new law, if passed, until the Home Team has been equipped?

sections.label: MHA clarifications on new law
sections.summary: MHA has issued at least three clarifications on the proposed new law in response to concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MHA has come forward with at least three clarifications that I am aware of on the proposed new law in response to concerns.

sections.label: Safe, inclusive, respectful Singapore
sections.summary: Speaker seeks assurances for persons in recovery, families, caregivers, mental health professionals and healthcare staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We want a Singapore that is both safe and at the same time inclusive and respectful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I trust the hon Minister will give us the assurances that not just Members in this House need but also to the persons in recovery, their families, their caregivers and the mental health professionals and healthcare staff.

sections.label: Police action and reasonable limits
sections.summary: The amendment clarifies Police need not wait for imminent danger, but limits of reasonable action must be understood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The amendment clarifies that the Police do not have to wait for an "imminent" danger before taking action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, it is also essential to understand the limits of what constitutes "reasonable" to prevent overreach.

sections.label: Singapore CREST teams count
sections.summary: Singapore has over 70 Community Resource, Engagement and Support Teams spread across various regions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Currently, Singapore boasts over 70 Community Resource, Engagement and Support Teams (CREST) spread across various regions.

sections.label: Police self-harm intervention powers
sections.summary: Question asks if the amendment lets Police intervene in self-harm attempts, with support instead of charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry confirm whether the amendment grants powers to the Police to intervene when someone attempts to self-harm, with the assurance that the individual is unlikely to face charges but will instead receive mental health support?

sections.label: Phishing simulation exercise Playbook use
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry would encourage those running phishing training exercises to use the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore's Playbook for the Conduct of Phishing Simulation Exercises.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Accordingly: would the Ministry consider encouraging individuals or organisations undertaking training exercises on phishing to use the Playbook for the Conduct of Phishing Simulation Exercises, as published by the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore?

sections.label: Risk of misleading cybersecurity warnings
sections.summary: Asks what strategies minimise the risk of individuals being misled or confused by genuine cybersecurity warnings and advice, given possible exploitation of the exemption.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the potential for bad actors to exploit this exemption: what strategies are in place to minimise the risk of individuals being misled or confused by genuine cybersecurity warnings and advice?

sections.label: Resources and training for Anti-Scam Command
sections.summary: Asks what resources, including training, are provided to the Anti-Scam Command to strengthen its expertise and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just last month, The Straits Times reported, and I quote: "More than 300 people are being investigated for their involvement in more than 1,000 scam cases in which victims lost over $11 million".

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On that note, I would like to clarify: what resources, including training, are being provided to the Anti-Scam Command (ASCom) to strengthen their expertise and capabilities?

sections.label: Police training on section 13 detention
sections.summary: Asks what training Police officers receive on section 13 detention as a last resort, on mental illness, on sensitive interaction, and what mechanisms protect apprehended persons' rights.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What training is being provided to Police officers to ensure they understand and comply with the legal requirement that people can only be detained under section 13 as a last resort and only when they pose a danger to themselves or others?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What training is being provided to Police officers to increase their understanding of mental illness and how people living with mental illness may present or behave?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What training is being provided to Police officers to increase their capacity to interact sensitively and appropriately with people living with mental illness?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And what mechanisms are in place to protect the rights of people apprehended under section 13, including their right to independent legal advice?

sections.label: Guideline for officers and intervention basis
sections.summary: States the changes give officers a clear guideline to act decisively and compassionately, and that potential risk of harm rather than imminence can be the basis for intervention.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Importantly, these changes aim to provide officers with a clear guideline, enabling them to act decisively and compassionately in situations where individuals may pose a risk to themselves or others.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, the potential risk of harm, rather than imminence, can be the basis for intervention.

sections.label: Police mental health and de-escalation training
sections.summary: Asks how Police officers are equipped with mental health awareness and de-escalation training for expanded powers, and whether apprehension processes would be periodically reviewed with mental health experts or the Mental Health Office.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To that end, I would like to ask how are our Police officers equipped with mental health awareness and knowledge and de-escalation training to use these expanded powers appropriately, with empathy and understanding?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider periodically reviewing apprehension processes with inputs from mental health experts or even the new Mental Health Office?

sections.label: Apprehension in attempted suicide cases
sections.summary: The new section 26AA lets the Police apprehend a person reasonably suspected to be about to attempt suicide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the concerns I shared, and the clarifications sought to quell misunderstandings, or rather, misinformation, that is being shared, I support the amendments to the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 26AA sets out the manner of apprehension in attempted suicide cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under this section, the Police may apprehend a person who is reasonably suspected to be about to attempt to commit suicide.

sections.label: Apprehending mentally disordered persons
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Police apprehend a mentally disordered person when there is a reasonable likelihood of danger to human life or personal safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces amendments to allow the Police to apprehend a mentally disordered person, when there is a reasonable likelihood of danger to human life or personal safety posed by the person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The danger does not have to be imminent and actual harm does not have to be caused.

sections.label: Rationale for new offences
sections.summary: A member asks the Minister for the rationale for new offences instead of existing abetment and conspiracy provisions, and whether they address legal gaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share the rationale for introducing new offences instead of relying on existing provisions for abetment and conspiracy offences?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Are the new provisions intended to address gaps in our laws where individuals could not be prosecuted because our laws were not precise enough to tackle that form of wrongdoing?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My concern is that we end up with a proliferation of laws which become too complicated to understand.

sections.label: Liability of SIM card subscribers
sections.summary: The new offences deem irresponsible subscribers and middlemen liable without proof of criminal intent or knowledge in certain scenarios.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With the new offences, we will deem irresponsible subscribers and middlemen liable for an offence, without needing to prove criminal intent or knowledge, in certain scenarios.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These include, among others, registering for a SIM card and selling it for gain; possessing a large number of unregistered SIM cards for no legitimate reason; and buying or selling SIM cards registered in another person's particulars.

sections.label: Commencement of new offences
sections.summary: The offences are intended to come into force about six months after the Bill is passed, to let the public familiarise themselves with them.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In any case, to allow members of the public to familiarise themselves with the new offences, we intend for the offences to come into force approximately six months after the Bill is passed.

sections.label: Scammers' local SIM card numbers
sections.summary: The Police have observed scammers possessing as few as 15 to 20 local SIM cards to send tens of thousands of scam SMSes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Police have observed cases of scammers possessing as few as 15 to 20 local SIM cards to send tens of thousands of scam SMSes.

sections.label: Subscribers with many postpaid SIM cards
sections.summary: A 2022 poll found about 2,000 subscribers, under 0.1%, registered more than 10 postpaid SIM cards with one provider.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Based on a 2022 poll of all mobile service providers, only about 2,000 subscribers, or less than 0.1% of all subscribers, used their own particulars to register for more than 10 postpaid SIM cards with a single mobile service provider.

sections.label: Liability of key officers
sections.summary: New sections 40A and 40B in the MOA allow key officers and senior management involved in the offence to be held liable.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Under the new sections 40A and 40B in the MOA, key officers and senior management who were involved in committing the offence can be held liable.

sections.label: Directions against accounts involved
sections.summary: Once the new offences come into force and second-hand local SIM card sales are illegal, directions may be considered under the Online Criminal Harms Act.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Once the new offences come into force and the second-hand sale of local SIM cards becomes illegal, we will consider issuing directions under the Online Criminal Harms Act to the platforms to require them to restrict access to accounts involved.

sections.label: Overseas scam syndicate take-downs
sections.summary: Police worked with overseas counterparts including Royal Malaysia Police and INTERPOL, leading to the take-down of 19 overseas scam syndicates in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Police have been working with our overseas counterparts, such as the Royal Malaysia Police and INTERPOL, to exchange information and conduct joint operations.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This has led to the successful take-down of 19 overseas scam syndicates in 2023.

sections.label: Genuine cybersecurity warnings excluded
sections.summary: Genuine cybersecurity warnings and advice are not within section 14D's scope because they are not false or fabricated messages.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To clarify, genuine cybersecurity warnings and advice do not fall within the scope of section 14D as they are not false or fabricated messages.

sections.label: Police involvement only when called
sections.summary: Police will not get involved unless called to prevent harm from happening.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As I explained at the start of the debate, Police will not get involved unless called to prevent harm from happening.

sections.label: Apprehension leads to medical assessment
sections.summary: A person apprehended under the MHCTA is brought to a medical practitioner for assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When an individual has been apprehended under the MHCTA, they will be brought to a medical practitioner for assessment.

sections.label: MHCTA apprehension not criminal offence
sections.summary: Apprehension under the MHCTA is not a criminal offence for which the person can be prosecuted.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To reiterate, apprehension under MHCTA is not a criminal offence for which the person can be prosecuted.

sections.label: Questions on Police accompaniment
sections.summary: Mr Ng, Assoc Prof Razwana, Dr Syed Harun and Mr Chua asked whether Police should be accompanied by mental health professionals or community first responders.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Ng, Assoc Prof Razwana, Dr Syed Harun and Mr Chua asked whether Police should be accompanied by mental health professionals or community first responders when responding to cases involving persons with mental health conditions.

sections.label: Police role and MHCTA basis
sections.summary: Police deal with threat of harm and protect public safety, so an officer's belief that a person is dangerous to himself suffices to apprehend.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Their role is to deal with the threat of harm and protect public safety.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is why the current MHCTA states that a Police officer’s belief that a person is doing or about to do an act which is dangerous to himself is sufficient basis for the officer to suspect that the danger to that person is attributable to a mental disorder and to apprehend the person.

sections.label: Resourcing and referral numbers
sections.summary: No significant increase in referrals is expected from the amendments because the threshold remains high.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To Mr Ng's question on resourcing, we do not expect a significant increase in the number of referrals as a result of the amendments because the threshold is still quite high as pointed out previously by Dr Syed Harun.

sections.label: CRPD compliance and Police response
sections.summary: The MHCTA remains CRPD-compliant after amendments, which do not affect Police response since such incidents are not criminal offences.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To Ms He's question on whether the amendments are in compliance with the CRPD, we can confirm that the MHCTA continues to be in compliance after the amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The amendment does not affect how the Police respond to such incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is because such incidents, in and of themselves, do not constitute criminal offences.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have explained the Government's view that neighbour disputes and noise complaints should be resolved through a community-based approach, where community partners, Government social or municipal agencies, and grassroots leaders work together to resolve the issues.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Police's resources should focus on the prevention, deterrence, and detection of crime.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They will respond to neighbour disputes and noise complaints only where there are law and order concerns.

sections.label: Apprehension versus arrest treatment
sections.summary: The Attorney-General submits there is no practical difference between apprehend and arrest, while the Minister stressed a difference, and treatment of apprehended and arrested persons differs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: At paragraph 30 in the High Court judgment, it states that the Attorney-General submits that there is no practical difference between the terms "apprehend" and "arrest", and a person is apprehended under section 7 of the MHCTA when he is compelled to accompany a Police officer to be examined by a medical practitioner.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: So, given that the Minister stressed earlier that there is a difference between apprehension and arrest, I would like to understand and seek clarification about the Attorney-General's submissions during the High Court case, and how that squares with what was said earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But what I was trying to get to is that the treatment of a person who is apprehended and a person who is arrested, from the Police's standpoint, is quite clearly different.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When a person is arrested, that next course of action is to bring them to a lock-up where they may then be investigated further.

sections.label: Apprehended person medical attention
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether an apprehended person is not taken to a police cell or lock-up but directly to seek medical attention.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Upon apprehension, can I just confirm that the person being apprehended does not actually get taken in a police cell, or into a lock-up, and instead, is directly taken down to seek medical attention?
